newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire, UK power stocks down on UBS note.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire, UK power stocks down on UBS note.

text.p: Shares in UK regional electricity stocks dropped on Monday as analysts at UBS issued a negative review of the sector including "fair value" estimates below the current market price of the shares, traders said.

Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc was down 11-1/2p at 756-1/2 by 1054 GMT, East Midlands Electricity Plc was off 8-1/2p at 566-1/2, London Electricity Plc down 8-1/2p at 621-1/2, Northern Electric Plc was down 8p at 529 and Southern Electric Plc was down 8-1/2p at 663-1/2.
UBS repeated "sell" ratings on London, Northern and Southern and "hold" ratings on East Midlands and Yorkshire.

They said their new fair value estimates had factored in an expected windfall tax if the opposition Labour Party, currently well ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls, wins the UK general election to be held by next May.

Assuming a one billion stg one-off tax on the electricity sector would mean Southern -- the biggest regional electricity company -- being subject to a bill of 103 million stg on the basis of its market capitalisation, UBS said.
After taking account of the tax, UBS put a fair value on London of 572p, on Northern of 460p, on Southern of 630p, on East Midlands of 545p and on Yorkshire of 700p.

The brokerage said the stocks continued to be supported by takeover hopes but warned that bid premia would progressively be eroded as the general election approaches and the expected windfall levy comes closer.

East Midlands and Yorkshire were not rated "sell" because they continue to be regarded as most likely -- or least unlikely -- bid targets and because of their better dividend prospects, analysts said.
